chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever eats seven Ajwa dates every day upon the empty stomach from the dates of Al-Aaliya, neither poison will harm him, nor sorcery, nor Satan.

key_terms.تَمْر الْعَالِيَة: Dates of Al-Aaliya: Refers to dates from a specific region or area in Medina known for quality.
key_terms.سِحْر: Sorcery/Magic: The practice of using supernatural forces to cause harm.
key_terms.شَيْطَان: Satan: The devil or evil spirit.
key_terms.عَجْوَة: Ajwa: A specific, highly regarded variety of date, particularly from Medina.
key_terms.عَلَى الرِّيق: Upon the empty stomach: Refers to eating before consuming other food or drink.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of eating seven Ajwa dates daily according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the dual spiritual and physical efficacy of Ajwa dates, a variety particularly revered in Shia tradition for their medicinal properties. The practice of consuming seven dates on an empty stomach (*ala al-riq*) serves as a comprehensive shield (*tadhkir*) against poison, sorcery, and the influence of Satan, reflecting the holistic view of health in Shia jurisprudence.
